title: Jesus: Historical Figure and Mythic Archetype
description: History, language, and myth—five scholarly depths on a world-changing figure.

questions.question: What execution method do virtually all historians agree was used on Jesus?
questions.explanation: Tacitus (c. 116 CE) writes that "Christus" suffered "the extreme penalty" under Pontius Pilate. With Paul's letters and the Gospels, it is among the best-attested facts of his life.

questions.question: The man Rome sentenced to crucifixion was named Yeshua. What does that Hebrew name mean?
questions.explanation: A short form of Yehoshua (Joshua), it ranked among the most common Jewish male names of the era. Matthew 1:21 plays on the meaning: "he will save his people."

questions.question: Matthew says a star marked the birth of the boy whose name means "God saves." A theory dating back to Kepler links it to which two planets?
questions.explanation: After seeing a 1604 supernova near those planets, Kepler proposed a new star tied to their 7 BCE triple conjunction in Pisces. Rival ideas: a comet, a nova, or a purely literary star.

questions.question: That Jupiter and Saturn sign is said to have drawn the Magi from the East—what were magi most likely by profession?
questions.explanation: Matthew never counts them: Origen inferred three from the three gifts, and "kings" came later via Psalm 72. Their Persian title, through Greek magos, gave us "magic."

questions.question: Matthew tells the priest-astronomers' story in a gospel. The Greek word behind it, "euangelion," literally means what?
questions.explanation: The word hailed emperors first: a c. 9 BCE inscription at Priene calls Augustus's birthday "the beginning of the good news for the world." Some scholars read Mark 1:1 as a counterclaim.
